source.title: Open problems of the 32nd Workshop on Cycles and Colourings

accepted.question_text: For every 3-connected cubic graph G, does there exist a blue-red vertex coloring whose blue induced subgraph B has maximum degree at most 1 and whose red induced subgraph R satisfies some weakened replacement for the failed crumby-coloring red conditions, namely minimum degree at least 1 and no path with 3 edges? Equivalently, what relaxation of the conditions imposed on the red induced subgraph R guarantees that such a blue-red coloring always exists for every 3-connected cubic graph?

evidence.quote: Problem 1.1 What relaxation of the conditions on R guarantees that such a coloring of a 3-connected cubic graph always exists?

accepted.question_text: Let G be a graph. A k-list-assignment L assigns k allowable colors to each vertex; a proper L-coloring chooses one allowed color at each vertex and gives adjacent vertices different colors; k proper L-colorings are pairwise disjoint if, at every vertex, all k chosen colors are distinct. Let χℓ(G) be the least k such that every k-list-assignment admits a proper L-coloring, and let χ⋆ℓ(G) be the least k such that every k-list-assignment admits an L-packing of size k. Does there exist a graph G for which χ⋆ℓ(G) is greater than χℓ(G)+1?

evidence.quote: Problem 2.1 Is there a graph G for which χ⋆ ℓ(G)> χ ℓ(G) + 1?

accepted.question_text: With χℓ(G) denoting the list-chromatic number of a graph G and χ⋆ℓ(G) denoting the least k such that every k-list-assignment of G admits k pairwise disjoint proper L-colorings, is the inequality χ⋆ℓ(G) ≤ 2χℓ(G) true for every graph G?

evidence.quote: Problem 2.2 Is it true that χ⋆ ℓ(G)≤2 χ ℓ(G)for every graph G?

accepted.question_text: For every cubic planar graph G and every 3-list-assignment L of G, is it always possible to choose two pairwise disjoint proper L-colorings, meaning two proper colorings from the same lists that assign different colors to each vertex?

evidence.quote: Problem 2.3 Is it possible to choose two disjoint proper colourings?

accepted.question_text: For every cubic planar graph G and every 3-list-assignment L of G, is it always possible to choose three pairwise disjoint proper L-colorings, meaning three proper colorings from the same lists that assign mutually different colors to each vertex?

evidence.quote: Problem 2.4 Is it possible to choose three disjoint proper colourings?

accepted.question_text: For every cubic bipartite graph G and every 3-list-assignment L of G, is it always possible to find three pairwise disjoint proper L-colorings?

evidence.quote: Hence, the following question arises: Is it possible to find three disjoint proper colourings in the case of cubic bipartite graphs?

accepted.question_text: For every graph G, is the list packing number χ⋆ℓ(G) at most Δ(G)+1, where Δ(G) is the maximum degree of G and χ⋆ℓ(G) is the least k such that every k-list-assignment of G admits k pairwise disjoint proper L-colorings?

evidence.quote: Problem 2.5 Is it true that χ⋆ ℓ(G)≤∆(G) + 1 for every graph G?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a planar graph G whose list packing number χ⋆ℓ(G) is at least 6, where χ⋆ℓ(G) is the least k such that every k-list-assignment of G admits k pairwise disjoint proper L-colorings?

evidence.quote: Problem 2.6 Is there a planar graph with χ⋆ ℓ(G)≥6?

accepted.question_text: Is χ⋆ℓ(G) ≤ 7 for every planar graph G, where χ⋆ℓ(G) is the least k such that every k-list-assignment of G admits k pairwise disjoint proper L-colorings?

evidence.quote: Problem 2.7 Is it true that χ⋆ ℓ(G)≤7 for every planar graph?

accepted.question_text: For every triangle-free planar graph G, is χ⋆ℓ(G) ≤ 4, where χ⋆ℓ(G) is the least k such that every k-list-assignment of G admits k pairwise disjoint proper L-colorings?

evidence.quote: Problem 2.8 For a triangle-free planar graph G, is it true that χ⋆ ℓ(G)≤4?

accepted.question_text: For every graph G and every vertex v of G, is χ⋆ℓ(G) ≤ χ⋆ℓ(G-v)+2, where χ⋆ℓ denotes the list packing number and G-v is the graph obtained by deleting v?

evidence.quote: Problem 2.9 Let v and e be a vertex and an edge of a graph G. Is it true that χ⋆ ℓ(G)≤ χ⋆ ℓ(G\v) + 2?

accepted.question_text: For every graph G and every edge e of G, is χ⋆ℓ(G) ≤ χ⋆ℓ(G-e)+2, where χ⋆ℓ denotes the list packing number and G-e is the graph obtained by deleting e?

evidence.quote: Or, is it true that χ⋆ ℓ(G)≤χ⋆ ℓ(G\e) + 2?

accepted.question_text: For each fixed integer k>2, is the decision problem that takes a graph G as input and asks whether the list packing number χ⋆ℓ(G) is at most k complete for the complexity class Π^P_2?

evidence.quote: Problem 2.10 Fix k > 2. Given a graph G as input, is the problem of deciding whether χ⋆ ℓ(G)≤k complete for the complexity class Π P 2?

accepted.question_text: For each fixed integer t>1, is there a polynomial-time algorithm that, given a graph G of treewidth at most t, determines the value of the list packing number χ⋆ℓ(G)?

evidence.quote: Problem 2.11 (Question 7.3 in [3]) Fix t > 1. Is the problem of determining the value of χ⋆ ℓ(G)or χ• ℓ(G), given a graph G of treewidth at most t as input, in P?

accepted.question_text: Let n=4k+1 for an integer k≥1, let S be a k-element subset of {1,2,...,2k}, and let the extended Petersen graph XP(2n,S) have vertex set Z_n×{1,2}, edges within the first layer determined by circular distances in S, edges within the second layer determined by the complementary set of distances, and matching edges joining the two copies of each x in Z_n. Apart from the Petersen graph itself, is every extended Petersen graph Class 1, meaning edge-colorable with Δ(G) colors?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3.1 (Horák, Rosa [1]) Every extended Petersen graph, except Petersen graph itself, is of Class 1.

accepted.question_text: For non-complete graphs G of order n, where δ(G) is the minimum degree and rc(G) is the rainbow connection number, does there exist a constant c≥0 such that δ(G) ≥ n/2+c always implies rc(G)=2? Here an edge-colored graph is rainbow connected if every two vertices are connected by a path whose edges all have different colors, and rc(G) is the minimum number of colors needed for such a coloring.

evidence.quote: Problem 4.1 Does there exist a constant c≥0 such that if G is a non-complete graph of order n with δ(G)≥n 2+c, then rc(G) = 2?

accepted.question_text: For every non-complete graph G of order n, does the minimum-degree condition δ(G) ≥ n/2 by itself imply that the rainbow connection number rc(G) equals 2?

evidence.quote: In particular, does δ(G)≥n 2 imply that rc(G) = 2?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a 5-edge-connected 5-regular graph that is Class 2, meaning it is not edge-colorable with Δ(G) colors?

evidence.quote: Problem 5.1 (Ma, Mattiolo, Steffen, Wolf [1]) Is there any 5-edge-connected 5-regular Class 2 graph?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a poorly matchable 5-edge-connected 5-graph? Here a 5-graph is a 5-regular graph in which every odd vertex set X has at least 5 edges to its complement, and poorly matchable means that any two perfect matchings intersect.

evidence.quote: Problem 5.2 Is there a poorly matchable 5-edge-connected 5-graph?

accepted.question_text: Can one describe exactly all subcubic K3-free graphs of Class 2, where subcubic means maximum degree at most 3, K3-free means triangle-free, and Class 2 means the graph is not edge-colorable with Δ(G) colors?

evidence.quote: Problem 6.1 Is it possible to describe all subcubic K 3-free graphs of Class 2?

accepted.question_text: Given a graph G, can it be decided in polynomial time whether G has a Type-A order or a Type-B order of its vertices? For a linear order v1,...,vn, d−(vi) is the number of neighbors of vi appearing earlier and d+(vi) is the number appearing later; a Type-A order requires every d−(v) to be odd or 0, while a Type-B order allows either that Type-A condition or the alternative that d−(v) is even and d+(v)=0.

evidence.quote: Problem 7.1 Can it be decided in polynomial time whether a graph G admits a Type-A order, or a Type-B order?

accepted.question_text: When a graph G has a Type-A order or a Type-B order, can such an order be found in polynomial time? A Type-A order requires each vertex to have an odd number of earlier neighbors or none, and a Type-B order additionally permits a vertex to have an even number of earlier neighbors if it has no later neighbors.

evidence.quote: Problem 7.2 If a Type-A or Type-B order exists, can it be found in polynomial time?

trace.notes: Original zbMATH URL resolved via the zbMATH REST API to arXiv:2411.10046, title 'Open problems of the 32nd Workshop on Cycles and Colourings'. Shell download of the arXiv PDF failed with DNS resolution error for arxiv.org, so an exact-title full-text HTML rendering on ResearchGate was used as the primary readable source.

Mapped seven source sections: crumby colorings; list packing; extended Petersen graphs; rainbow connectivity; 5-edge-connected 5-regular graphs; subcubic K3-free Class 2 graphs; special vertex orderings.
Extracted one crumby-coloring relaxation problem.

Extracted list-packing Problems 2.1-2.11, split the compound deletion question into vertex-deletion and edge-deletion items, extracted the implicit cubic-bipartite question, and separated the undefined χ•ℓ bounded-treewidth subquestion for review.
Extracted the Horák-Rosa conjecture on extended Petersen graphs as an open question.
Extracted the rainbow-connectivity constant-threshold problem and its explicit n/2-threshold subquestion.
Extracted questions on 5-edge-connected 5-regular Class 2 graphs and poorly matchable 5-graphs.
Extracted the classification problem for subcubic K3-free Class 2 graphs.
Extracted decision and construction questions for Type-A and Type-B vertex orders.
Expanded 'such a coloring' by naming G, B, R, and the crumby-coloring red conditions.
Inlined list assignment, proper L-coloring, disjointness, χℓ, and χ⋆ℓ definitions.
Rewrote the linear-bound question with χℓ and χ⋆ℓ definitions.
Expanded 'two disjoint proper colourings' in the setting of a 3-list-assignment of a cubic planar graph.
Expanded 'three disjoint proper colourings' in the setting of a 3-list-assignment of a cubic planar graph.
Captured the implicit cubic-bipartite three-coloring-packing question.
Restated the maximum-degree upper-bound question with Δ(G) and χ⋆ℓ context.
Restated the planar lower-bound existence question.
Restated the planar upper-bound question.
Restated the triangle-free planar upper-bound question.
Split the vertex-deletion inequality from Problem 2.9.
Split the edge-deletion inequality from Problem 2.9.
Restated the fixed-k Π^P_2-completeness question.
Accepted the χ⋆ℓ bounded-treewidth computation subquestion; the χ•ℓ subquestion was moved to review.
Expanded the extended Petersen graph definition and Class 1 meaning.
Expanded rainbow path, rainbow connected, rc(G), δ(G), and order n.
Separated the explicit δ(G)≥n/2 subquestion from the constant-c version.
Expanded Class 2 as failure of Δ(G)-edge-colorability.
Inlined r-graph and poorly matchable definitions for r=5.
Expanded subcubic, K3-free, and Class 2 terminology.
Inlined d−, d+, Type-A order, and Type-B order definitions for the decision problem.
Inlined Type-A and Type-B order definitions for the construction problem.
No near-duplicate rewritten questions were merged. Compound source problems were split only when they stated distinct mathematical or algorithmic questions.

Accepted q_001 through q_022 after self-containedness, evidence coverage, evidence completeness, no-new-facts, source adequacy, and schema checks. All accepted questions have is_solved=false because the source does not mark any of them solved.
Moved to needs_review because χ•ℓ(G) is used in the source but not defined in the visible primary source text, so a self-contained rewrite would require unsupported terminology.
